title: Impeller
model_title: Closed Centrifugal Pump Impeller (6 Backward-Curved Vanes)

introduction.definition: A centrifugal pump impeller is a rotating wheel with curved vanes between a back shroud and a front shroud. Liquid enters at the eye, is turned outward through the vane passages and leaves the rim with higher pressure and velocity. Back vanes and balance holes reduce axial thrust; the impeller is dynamically balanced.
applications: All centrifugal pumps (water, process, slurry with open/semi-open types)
introduction.summary: A centrifugal pump impeller is a rotating wheel with curved vanes between two shrouds. It takes liquid in at the eye and throws it outward, adding pressure and velocity.

pressure.title: Pressure and velocity rise outward
pressure.description: Liquid enters the eye axially, turns into the vane passages and is flung outward. The vanes add angular momentum (Euler: H ≈ u₂·c_u2 / g), so both pressure and velocity rise from eye to tip; the volute or diffuser then converts much of the velocity into pressure. Backward-curved vanes give a stable, falling head curve. Head scales with tip speed squared (u₂ = π·D·n), so trimming the diameter lowers head (affinity laws). Shrouds, balance holes and back vanes manage leakage and axial thrust; the impeller is dynamically balanced (e.g. ISO 21940 G6.3).

video_tutorials.title: Impeller — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Impeller.
A centrifugal pump impeller is a rotating wheel with curved vanes between a back shroud and a front shroud.
Liquid enters at the eye, is turned outward through the vane passages and leaves the rim with higher pressure and velocity.
Back vanes and balance holes reduce axial thrust; the impeller is dynamically balanced.
Typical applications include all centrifugal pumps (water, process, slurry with open/semi-open types); fans and compressors (similar principle).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Impeller: Hub, Back Shroud, Vanes & Front Shroud (turning), Shaft & Key (drive the impeller), Pump-Out (Back) Vanes — reduce pressure behind the impeller and axial thrust.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Impeller — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Impeller.
Trend vibration and performance.
Inspect for erosion / cavitation.
Repair or replace; rebalance.
Watch for cavitation damage: noise, pitted vanes. Common cause: low NPSHa.
Watch for imbalance: 1× vibration. Common cause: erosion, deposits.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
